source.repro: pnpm exec esbuild --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --target=node22 --outfile=/tmp/lanestab.mjs plugins/linear-comparative-view/benches/multiwayLaneStability.probe.ts && node /tmp/lanestab.mjs, from the repo root (it rewrites this file) - the deployed demos/grape_peach_cacao MCScan blocks track over the network, grape chr1 (NC_081805.1), a 2Mb window walked in 100kb steps, 259 steps, 1280px, each step's decision carried into the next the way the display carries a settle's into the next settle.
source.notes:
WHICH OF A LANE'S PER-SETTLE CHOICES HOLD STILL WHILE THE ANCHOR PANS. `decideLaneFrames` decides four things per settle - contig, orientation, ladder rung and placement - and every one now has an incumbent: the contig by `preferIncumbent`'s switch margin, the cluster the fit is centred on by the same rule (`keepNearMedian` takes the incumbent centre), the rung by a shrink room, the orientation by the follow's NEARLY_ALL deadband over at least five shared groups and carried across a contig change, the placement by coverage of the placed weight.

A CHANGE IS NOT A FLICKER, and the two are counted apart: a lane moving from one syntenic block to the next changes once and stays, which is the data; a lane on a near-tie leaves a value and comes back. `osc` counts only the second, within a fifth of a window.

RE-MEASURED 2026-09-06 after `orientationVote` changed from neighbour pairs weighed by the lighter run to every pair weighed by the product of group weights: the same bundle with the old rule patched back reproduces the 2026-09-02 table exactly (drawn flip changes 3/4/5/7/8/2, every osc 0), and the new rule is worse on every lane - drawn flip changes 5/7/12/9/14/9 and drawn flip oscillations 0/0/3/2/2/2 (peach, citrus, cacao, poplar, tomato, arabidopsis). Contig, rung and fallback columns are unchanged; the slip columns moved because fewer steps sit on one orientation. On a gene table every group weighs one, so the product vote is a plain concordance over every pair of shared genes, and a paleopolyploid lane holding two interleaved blocks reads close to even under it where the neighbour rule read the runs.

THE 2026-09-02 TABLE, before the vote change: EVERY OSC COLUMN WAS ZERO. The stateless version of the same walk (2026-08-26, earlier the same day) had contig oscillations only on arabidopsis (3 of 12 changes), drawn flip changes of 10-21 per lane with 1-7 oscillations, and rungs that swung between 1 and 3 on consecutive steps on cacao as `keepNearMedian`'s median hopped between two paleo-blocks. Flip changes are 3-8 now; `fallback` is the anchor-order sign sum a fresh lane falls back on, kept as the control and never applied over an incumbent.

WHAT THE DEADBAND ALONE DID NOT CLOSE: a contig change used to reset the orientation to that fallback, which the vote then corrected a step later (poplar, tomato); three reversed genes could mirror a whole lane (tomato at a 26kb fit); and the rung oscillated because the cluster the fit keeps is a discrete choice too. Each got its own incumbent.

`empty` is windows where the lane places nothing at all - a low-synteny stretch of grape chr1, the same 33 for every lane.
